item.title: NVIDIA Releases Kumo Forecast for Multi-Variate Time-Series Forecasting
item.description:
NVIDIA Releases Kumo Forecast for Multi-Variate Time-Series Forecasting

NVIDIA has introduced Kumo Forecast (formerly known as NV-Tesseract Forecasting), a multi-variate time-series forecasting model that integrates a pretrained Transformer backbone with a context-enhanced retrieval mode.

🧩 How it works

Kumo-Forecast combines four main components to generate predictions by drawing on representations learned during pretraining and historical observations available for the current application:

Component Function
Pretrained Temporal Encoder Uses the MOMENT-1-large Transformer encoder as the backbone.
Trainable Forecasting Head Maps representations to future values for the requested horizon.
Historical-Pattern Retrieval Uses a nearest-neighbor approach to retrieve related patterns from historical data.
Interpretability Framework Produces model-agnostic explanations without modifying the forecaster.

⚙️ Key details

  • Architecture: The model uses a MOMENT-1-large backbone consisting of an approximately 340-million-parameter base encoder. During training of the forecasting head, the encoder and embedder weights remain frozen.
  • Forecasting Modes:
    • Direct Forecasting: Uses the MOMENT-based Transformer and forecasting head to predict future values, with support for autoregressive extension for horizons beyond native capability.
    • Domain-Aware Representation and Retrieval (DARR): Augments direct forecasts by retrieving patterns from a separate historical DataFrame (context_df). Developers can configure the strength of reliance on each pathway.
  • Input Specifications: Supports input sequence lengths of 256, 512, 1024, and 2048 observations. Inputs must include a timestamp column and one or more numeric value columns via CSV, JSON, or pandas DataFrame.
  • Interpretability: When enabled, the framework provides an explanation bundle including trajectory-stability diagnostics, semantic-flow diagnostics, lag and feature attributions per horizon, and optional embedding Integrated Gradients.

🚀 Availability

  • License: Available under the Apache 2.0 license.
  • API: Provides a DataFrame-first API with configurable forecast horizons.
  • Integration: The Predictive Maintenance module within the Factory Operations (FOX) Blueprint leverages Kumo Forecast and Kumo Anomaly to predict future anomalies from real-time data.
  • Developer Resources: The Kumo-TS repository includes examples for fine-tuning the model on user-supplied CSVs, supporting both pretrained inference and adaptation workflows.

#NVIDIA #TimeSeries #Forecasting #MachineLearning #Transformer

Source: NVIDIA Kumo Forecast Combines Pretrained Time-Series Representations with Historical Pattern Retrieval and Interpretability

item.title: NVIDIA Earth-2 Introduces AI Data Assimilation for Localized Weather Forecasting
item.description:
NVIDIA Earth-2 Introduces AI Data Assimilation for Localized Weather Forecasting

NVIDIA Earth-2 now includes AI data assimilation tools that allow organizations to process observations more efficiently and incorporate proprietary or third-party data into weather forecasting pipelines.

💡 Why it matters

Weather-sensitive industries use these tools to manage physical risk and improve operational decisions. Capabilities include:

  • Increased Frequency: Issuing forecasts more frequently than fixed-schedule numerical analyses.
  • Real-time Alignment: Keeping estimates aligned with real-time conditions.
  • Localization: Tailoring pipelines to specific regions, such as transmission corridors, production sites, or densely populated areas.
  • Sector Application: Supporting capital markets, insurance, agriculture, logistics, and energy production.

🧩 How it works

Score-Based Data Assimilation (SDA) is used to integrate observations into diffusion-based AI forecasting and downscaling models, such as StormCast and CorrDiff.

  • Consistent Predictions: SDA guides models toward predictions consistent with observations without requiring the model to be retrained.
  • The Denoising Process: Diffusion models generate high-resolution predictions via denoising steps; at each step, SDA compares intermediate predictions with observations to nudge the model.
  • Observation Operators: To nudge the model, an observation operator maps model output to the expected quantity at a measurement location. This can be:
    • Direct: Interpolating nearby grid values for physical quantities like wind speed or temperature.
    • Proxy: Using observed impacts, such as using wind turbine power output as a proxy for wind speed.
  • Probabilistic Output: Results show less uncertainty near observation locations and a wider spread further away, where predictions rely on AI simulations and other model inputs.

⚙️ Key details

  • Performance Factors: The effectiveness of SDA depends on the accuracy, number, and spatial distribution of observations, the quality of the observation operator, and the characteristic length scales of the predicted field.
  • Example Implementation: Using Earth2Studio, a pretrained CorrDiff model for Europe can turn 0.25° weather fields into 2.2-km predictions. In a test case limited to northwestern Germany and part of the Netherlands, 10-meter wind speeds were assimilated using GHCN wind observations and ERA5 data for low-resolution conditioning.

#NVIDIA #Earth-2 #WeatherForecasting #AIDataAssimilation #DiffusionModels

Source: Turn Your Latest Observations Into Timely Weather Decisions With NVIDIA Earth-2 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
